what_it_does: Many AI and scientific computations are expressed as 'einsum' operations — a compact notation for summing products across multiple arrays (tensors) at once, like a generalized dot product across many dimensions. When several such operations are chained together, there are two separate choices to make: in what order to do the pairwise multiplications (the contraction path), and how to arrange the numbers in memory for each intermediate result (the data layout). Researchers have previously studied each problem independently, leading to plans that may be locally efficient but globally wasteful. This paper introduces Einsum Trees, an intermediate representation that encodes the entire chain of operations as a tree, so that memory layout can be optimized globally across all intermediate steps at once. Tested on standard server processors (both Arm and x86 architectures), the approach reduces unnecessary data movement and improves use of the CPU's fast on-chip cache.
